body.text: Xi Jinping has returned to the White House for a state dinner hosted by Donald Trump, joined by some of the biggest names in tech, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang, Apple's Tim Cook and OpenAI's Sam Altman.
Both leaders are expected to deliver remarks in the East Room.
The dinner caps a day of pomp and closed-door diplomacy, which began with a welcome ceremony and military review for Mr Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan.
The two leaders held talks on issues including artificial intelligence, Iran and the Middle East, Ukraine and the Korean Peninsula.

Leaders expected to speak shortly
Both Trump and Xi are expected to address the dinner before enjoying a rather fancy meal.
Those in the East Room include some of the biggest names in business and tech including OpenAI's Sam Altman, Apple's Tim Cook and Nvidia's Jensen Huang.
Who is Xi's wife Peng Liyuan?

Xi Jinping's wife Peng Liyuan was already a hugely popular folk and classical singer in China, making regular appearances at state TV galas while Xi spent decades working his way up through local and central government.
They married in 1987 in what was an "arts meet politics" match.
On his visit to China in May this year, Trump did not bring First Lady Melania Trump and Madame Peng did not appear at any events.
The last time the two first ladies appeared together at an official event was during Trump's first visit to China in November 2017.
During that trip, "first ladies' diplomacy" was on full display, with the pair taking part in a series of carefully choreographed cultural and social events alongside the formal political talks.

As their husbands held bilateral talks, Ms Trump and Madame Peng visited the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art to explore works spanning centuries of artistic achievement and Sino-American cultural exchange.
How is this meeting being framed in China?
Unsurprisingly, there is plenty of glowing coverage in Chinese state media about Xi's trip to meet Trump.
Across TV and newspapers, there seems to be a consistent tone that this summit will help to cement a new era of "strategic stability" in US-Sino relations.
Op-eds running in state media also echo Xi's calls that "China and the US should be partners, not rivals".
"The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand, complement each other and benefit the world," says the state media Global Times.
Trump mocks Biden in front of Xi
A video has been posted by the White House of Trump showing Xi portraits of former presidents earlier in the day.
"Trump and then Trump," the US president said, pointing to images of himself.
"And this is the autopen," he said, pointing at a picture of an autopen in place of Joe Biden's portrait.
US presidents have used autopens to sign official documents for decades but Trump has repeatedly accused Biden of using one excessively — which Biden denies.
Trump greets Xi at White House
Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan have been met by Donald Trump and his wife Melania Trump at the White House.
A military band welcomed them, before handshakes and the obligatory photoshoot.
Journalists shouted questions at both leaders but neither responded as they walked toward the East Room of the White House.
Before their arrival, anti-China protests could be heard chanting from outside the White House.
Trump says meeting 'great'
Trump earlier hailed the "truly great friendship" he says he has built with Xi since 2016.
He made the comment as the two leaders delivered opening remarks ahead of a bilateral meeting.
Speaking to reporters after the talk, Trump brushed away questions about their policy discussions.
"Great meeting," he said.
What's on the menu?
The menu for the lavish dinner has been released by the White House.
It combines American ingredients with subtle Chinese influences:
• Welcome toast: Schramsberg "Blanc de Noir".
• First course: Yellow squash velouté, wild mushroom fricassée, crispy pancetta and scallion oil.
• Second course: Sesame-crusted sea bass, braised baby bok choy, roasted garden eggplant and sauce verte.
• Dessert: Vanilla crémeux and White House honey ice cream, walnut frangipane and sour cherry confit.
The welcome toast features the same American sparkling wine served at the 1972 "Toast to Peace" between then-US president Richard Nixon and then-Chinese premier Zhou Enlai.
The evening's entertainment will include performances by US military musicians, including the US Marine Band, Marine Drum and Bugle Corps, Army Chorus and Army Strings.
The headline performer will be classically trained tenor Christopher Macchio, who also performed at Trump's 2025 presidential inauguration.
The East Room will be decorated predominantly in red, drawing on the colour's longstanding cultural significance in China, with red flowers, linens and seasonal dahlias and ranunculus.
Two giant pandas to arrive at Atlanta Zoo 'within days': Xi
During his welcome address earlier, Xi said two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, would arrive at Atlanta Zoo in the coming days.
He described the pandas as "envoys of friendship" between the Chinese and American people.
The pair, a male and a female, were born at the Chengdu Research Base.
Atlanta Zoo previously hosted giant pandas from 1999 until 2024, when its last four pandas were returned to China amid a broader wind-down of the US panda-loan program.
Panda diplomacy dates back decades, with China using loans of the animals to signal warmth in its relations with other countries, most notably the US since the 1970s.
The practice has ebbed and flowed alongside the broader state of bilateral ties.
More big-name arrivals
The business and tech leaders continue to arrive at the White House.
Where is Xi's state dinner being held?
The state dinner will be held in the East Room of the White House, rather than the new State Ballroom, which is still under construction.
Trump had hoped to have the new ballroom ready for Xi's visit.

The new ballroom, being built on the site of the White House's former East Wing, is designed to provide a much larger space for state dinners and major events, accommodating between 650 and 1,000 guests.

Trump attended a state banquet with Xi in May at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. After returning to the US, he compared the two venues, calling China's hall a "serious hall", but his new ballroom would "top it."

The ballroom has also faced legal challenges. A federal appeals court previously blocked construction, ruling that congressional approval was required. The US Supreme Court later allowed construction to continue while the broader legal dispute proceeds.
The ballroom is expected to be completed later this year.
Protesters gather outside White House
As preparations continue for the state dinner, pro-Tibet and pro-Chinese Communist Party protesters have gathered outside the White House.
Business titans to join the state dinner
The full Chinese guest list for the state dinner hasn't been released yet.
On the American side, some of the biggest names in business and technology expected to attend include:
• Mary Barra — General Motors CEO
• Albert Bourla — Pfizer CEO
• Mark Zuckerberg — Meta Platforms Chief Executive
• Jeff Bezos — Amazon Founder
• Sundar Pichai — Alphabet (Google) CEO
• Sam Altman — OpenAI CEO
• Tim Cook — Apple Executive Chairman
• Elon Musk — Tesla CEO
• Jensen Huang — Nvidia CEO
• Michael Dell — Dell Technologies Founder and CEO
• Jamie Dimon — JPMorgan Chase CEO
• Jane Fraser — Citigroup CEO
Business and tech leaders arrive for state dinner
Some of the most influential leaders in US tech and business are set to attend the state dinner at the White House.
A few of them have just started to arrive.
US-China competition should have limits: Xi
Xi also called on the US and China to manage their differences and keep competition within bounds.
He said the competition between the two powers "should be virtuous and bounded", describing it as "a race of catching up with one another, not a wrestle in which one either wins or loses".
He said the so-called "Thucydides Trap" could be avoided.
Xi also announced China will invite 100,000 American teenagers to visit and study there over the next five years.
Xi calls for stable US-China ties
Xi addressed the welcome ceremony at the White House earlier.
He once again called for the United States and China to build a relationship with "constructive strategic stability", according to China's state news agency Xinhua.
Xi said the two countries had a historic responsibility to promote human development and progress amid global changes.
He said he was ready to work with Trump to steer the relationship towards stable and sustained development.
Xi outlined three priorities: strengthening communication, pursuing sincere cooperation and maintaining peaceful coexistence.
Trump media ban overturned
CNN, Politico and MS NOW journalists who Donald Trump banned from the White House are now back on the grounds.
A judge overnight ordered that their access be reinstated immediately, deeming the White House's decision likely unconstitutional.
But this morning in DC, journalists from those outlets were still denied entry and some had their passes confiscated — despite the judge's ruling.
It led to the outlets requesting an emergency hearing in court and around lunch time the reporters were allowed back in.
I've spent the early afternoon set up next to MS NOW as the journalists cross live retelling their experiences trying to get back into the White House.
Strong security presence at White House
Security around the White House is extremely tight and noticeably stricter than when Trump has hosted other foreign dignitaries.
There are multiple road closures and check points in place where you are required to show your credentials. Around the White House complex it's teeming with Secret Service and Chinese authorities.
During the welcome ceremony I could see multiple snipers set up along rooftops as well as other personnel on the ground.
This is all to be expected when two of the most powerful leaders meet in the one place but nevertheless it's quite the spectacle and disruption for everyday workers in DC.
What's happened so far?
While most of us in Australia slept, Xi and Trump held meetings in Washington.
China's president told Trump that AI must stay in human control and that he wanted better communication with the US military.
Chinese state media also reported that the pair discussed Taiwan and Iran.
There was of course plenty of pomp and ceremony too to welcome Xi to the White House.
